hints.title: Sign Count Allocation
hints.text: Notice that an alternating sequence of length n contains ceil(n / 2) positive terms and floor(n / 2) negative terms.

hints.title: Greedy Sorting Principle
hints.text: To maximize the result, assign the largest squares to the positive coefficients and the smallest squares to the negative coefficients.

hints.title: Direct Array Sorting
hints.text: Sort the array descendingly; add the squares of the first ceil(n / 2) elements and subtract the remainder.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def maxAlternatingSumOfSquares(self, nums: list[int]) -> int:
        # Choose order of nums to maximize alternating sum: x0^2 - x1^2 + x2^2 - x3^2 ...
        # Number of positive terms: ceil(n / 2)
        # Number of negative terms: floor(n / 2)
        # Assign largest values to positive terms, smallest values to negative terms
        sorted_nums = sorted(nums, reverse=True)
        n = len(nums)
        pos_count = (n + 1) // 2
        pos_terms = sorted_nums[:pos_count]
        neg_terms = sorted_nums[pos_count:]
        return sum(x * x for x in pos_terms) - sum(y * y for y in neg_terms)
```

variables: N: number of elements in nums
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Evaluating all N! permutations is completely intractable.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognize positive/negative sign counts and apply greedy partition.
